Graphing exercise using data on the costs of hundreds of rail projects around the world. Data is downloaded from TidyTuesday.[^1] Data is courtesy of the Transit Costs Project.[^2]

[^1]: Harmon, Jon. (2021, January 5). *Transit Costs Project*. TidyTuesday. <https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/main/data/2021/2021-01-05/readme.md>

[^2]: Transit Costs Project. (n.d.). NYU Marron Institute. <https://transitcosts.com/data/>

```{r}
#| out-width: 70%
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-alt: "A bar chart showing the cost per kilometer of building rail in different countries."

library(tidyverse)

#Borrowed from TidyTuesday instructions
transit_cost <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2021/2021-01-05/transit_cost.csv')

country_total <- transit_cost |>
  group_by(country) |>
  filter(country == "US" |
         country == "CN" |
         country == "BR" |
         country == "FR" |
         country == "AE") |>
  summarize(cost_km_millions = mean(cost_km_millions))

ggplot(country_total, aes(x = country, y = cost_km_millions, fill = country)) +
  geom_col() +
    labs(
    title = "Transit Infrastructure Project Costs by Country",
    x = "Country Code",
    y = "Cost Per KM in Millions of USD"
  ) +
  
  #Centered format
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
